thread:
marie (AE): Heads-up — Acme Corp asked for a POC to replace their current vendor with Redwood. They want prompt/response parity and security sign-offs before Q3 deal close. Who can lead technical coordination?
jamal (SE): I can own the compatibility checklist. Quick questions: do they need exact textual parity or semantic parity?
marie (AE): They said 'behavior parity' across our API surface, but legal insists on some deterministic parity tests for billing and regulatory mapping.
leo (Solutions Eng): Let's split: 1) API shim mapping (field/param translation) 2) prompt parity test harness 3) response delta analysis + tolerance matrix 4) security questionnaire response.
jamal (SE): For shim: competitor has a `conversation_id` field and different streaming frames. We should provide a tiny adapter example. Snippet: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/conv -d '{"conv_id": "123", "messages": [...]} '`
jamal (SE): Also note: competitor uses slightly different tokenization which causes token counts to differ. We'll surface token cost as a delta under pricing.
oliver (Eng-ML): For parity tests I recommend a 2k-prompt sampler across their production prompts, run side-by-side on our tuned quantized model and their model. Metrics: 1) intent_match_rate >= 95% 2) answer_semantic_similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.9 3) top1 identical >= 80% for high-confidence prompts. We'll also capture generation latency p95.
nina (Security): Security blockers: SSO (SAML) integration, VPC peering or Private deployment, KMS/HSM for keys, audit log export, and data residency. Acme will send a 40-page questionnaire — need owners to fill parts.
sara (Customer Success): I'll shepherd the questionnaire with Acme and own expectations. Suggest we ask for 2-week window for their security/compliance team to review.
leo (Solutions Eng): Operational checklist and owners: 1) Data flow diagram (nina) 2) API shim example + docs (jamal) 3) Parity harness + eval scripts (oliver) 4) Pricing delta calc (marie + jamal) 5) Runbook for failover to fallback model (leo).
marie (AE): Pricing note from procurement: they want an estimate for 3 scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved for baseline throughput, and private with on-prem license. Jamal — can you draft ballpark numbers (tokens/month + $) by EOD tomorrow?
jamal (SE): Yep. I'll do three scenarios. I'll include assumptions: avg token per request, expected qps, and expected caching hit rate (we should recommend enabling prefix caching).
oliver (Eng-ML): A couple of gotchas: quantized models can slightly alter punctuation/spacing, which may break exact-string checks. Recommend we avoid strict equality checks — use semantic or normalized-string checks. Also test function/tool-calling edge cases.
leo (Solutions Eng): Proposed acceptance criteria for POC sign-off: - parity metrics pass on sampled prompts - SSO + network controls verified in staging - performance SLO: p95 latency < 350ms for target qps - documentation and runbook handed to their infra team.
marie (AE): Great. Can we pencil in a 30-min kickoff with Acme + our tech leads tomorrow 11am PT? I'll send invite.
sara (Customer Success): +1. I'll be on the call to track questionnaire progress.
nina (Security): I'll join but may need to escalate some items to compliance for SOC2/KY3P checks.
jamal (SE): I'll prepare the shim sample and a short test plan. If anyone has golden prompts from Acme already, DM them to me.
marie (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll post the invite and attach Acme's initial security packet when I get it. :thumbsup:
leo (Solutions Eng): Quick FYI — if we need to demonstrate traffic mirroring for parity, eng-runtime can spin a small mirror, but we need signoff for extra capacity.
jamal (SE): noted. tagging @oliver and @nina for any model-level or security caveats.
marie (AE): last: timeline target — POC in 2 weeks, decision within 6 weeks. If anything blocks that, flag now.
